mechanism_narrative: A higher-than-trend FEDFUNDS rate coincides with elevated consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), reducing expected future rate cuts and pushing S&P 500 20-day returns downward.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS_TREND and CPIAUCSL > CPIAUCSL_TREND over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from a no-inflation, steady-funds-rate regime (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) simultaneously signal a strong labor market, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > PAYEMS_TREND and UNRATE < UNRATE_TREND over the prior 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns under strong labor conditions are not significantly higher than during weak labor periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend suggests expanding economic demand, which elevates equity valuations and yields positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO above trend does not translate into statistically significant positive 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) indicates softening supply constraints, lowering risk premia and producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly lower than during strong supply conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) coincides with a sharp rise in the federal funds rate, signaling tighter credit conditions that depress equity valuations and drive negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < HOUST_TREND and FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS_TREND over the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns during such conditions are not statistically worse than during loose-credit periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in unemployment (UNRATE) without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market, which can drive positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < UNRATE_TREND for 4 consecutive months and PAYEMS does not exceed TREND
failure_condition: 60-day returns under tight labor market are not significantly higher than in loose markets (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months is expected to lower growth expectations and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during periods of similar or lower rates (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend, coupled with rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL), indicates supply-side stress that elevates risk aversion and drives negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO_TREND and CPIAUCSL > CPIAUCSL_TREND over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 5-day returns during such events are not significantly worse than during normal supply conditions (p > 0.05).
